topic: Daily height loss: spinal disc compression, overnight recovery, astronaut growth
hook: You're shorter tonight than this morning
caption:
You are not the same height you were this morning. Gravity squeezes fluid out of the discs in your spine all day. By evening, most adults are about 1% shorter, which is often 1 to 2 cm.

The good news is that you get it all back overnight while you sleep. In space there is no gravity to squeeze them, so astronauts come home up to 3% taller for a while (Spine journal, NASA).

Follow for one fact about your body you never noticed, every day. Would you measure yourself tonight to check?

1/5 Blame your spine
Soft discs sit between your vertebrae. All day, gravity slowly squeezes fluid out of them.
🎨 AI-generated image

2/5 The daily shrink (-1%)
Studies measuring adults morning and evening found they lose about 1% of their height by night.
🎨 AI-generated image

3/5 Fastest after waking
Most of the loss happens in the first hours after you get out of bed and start moving.
📷 Markus Spiske (CC0 / public domain) via openverse

4/5 Sleep resets it
Lying down takes the load off. Overnight, the discs soak fluid back up and you regain your height.
🎨 AI-generated image

5/5 Astronauts grow (+3%)
With no gravity pressing down, the spine stretches out. Astronauts can grow up to 3% taller in space.
📷 NASA Johnson Space Center (Public domain) via wikimedia
